transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. What brings you in to see me today?

I’m here because… lately, when I have to be near scaffolding or a roof edge, even an upper platform, I get this feeling like I’m about to go over. I can see the rails are there, I know it’s supposed to be safe, but my head doesn’t really accept it.
Is it only heights that trigger this feeling, or are there other situations that cause you similar anxiety?

It’s really just the height-related stuff. Scaffolds, roof edges, upper platforms… places like that. Even when the rails are there and I know it’s set up safely, my head still says I’m going to go over.
Do you experience anxiety in situations other than those involving heights?
No… not really. It’s the height stuff. Scaffolds, roof edges, upper platforms. Even when I can see the rails are there, my head still tells me I’m about to go over.
How long have you been experiencing this fear of heights?
About thirteen months now… since that stair tower accident.
Do you feel anxious when you're in a height-related situation because you think you might actually fall, or because you're afraid of the feeling of falling itself?
It’s more that I think I’m actually going to fall. Like… I can see the rails, I know it’s supposed to be safe, but if I’m near a scaffold or roof edge, my head just says I’m about to go over.
Does this fear of falling occur when you're alone near heights or can it also happen when you're with someone you trust?

It can happen either way. If I have to go up, I usually want someone right beside me… someone I trust. I still rush through it scared, though. Mostly I’ve been handing those height inspections off to my foremen or moving meetings down to ground level.
Has this fear of heights affected your work or daily activities in any significant way?

Yeah… it has. I’ve put off or missed enough upper-level walk-throughs that the crews started second-guessing my calls. Subcontractors too.

And, uh… my employer’s insurer wanted an occupational health review because I wasn’t getting some of the safety inspections done. So it’s become a problem.
Do you ever get this feeling of falling when you're not actually near a height, like in a dream or just thinking about it?
I don’t think so. Not really. It’s more when I’m actually up there or close to an edge. Thinking about it isn’t great, but it’s not the same.
Do you think you would have this fear of falling if you were in a situation where you couldn't see the height, like being in a completely enclosed space on a high floor?

If I couldn’t see it? I don’t know… maybe not as much.

It’s really when I’m near a scaffold, roof edge, or platform and I can see where the drop is. Even with rails up, even knowing it’s supposed to be safe, my head just tells me I’m going to go over.
Is it the sight of the height that triggers your fear, rather than just being at a high place?
Yeah… mostly. If I can see the drop—like a scaffold edge or roof edge—that’s when it hits. Even if the rails are there and I know it’s supposed to be safe, my head goes straight to, “I’m going over.”
